one_line: An artisan-patron from ancient Dharanikota-Amaravati, shaping and sponsoring limestone reliefs for the great mahacetiya on the Krishna River.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, lean and wiry build from manual stone work
appearance.face: oval face with medium-brown Andhra complexion, straight nose, sharp but kind eyes, neatly kept short beard and moustache, calm focused expression as if mid-design.
appearance.hair: thick black hair parted slightly off-center, combed back and tied into a short, low knot at the nape; a simple narrow white cotton headband wraps horizontally around the forehead, keeping hair back while he works.
appearance.costume: A region-accurate Andhra artisan-patron outfit: upper body covered by a finely woven plain off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and across the chest, falling to mid-thigh; beneath it a close-wrapped light beige cotton tunic-like undergarment with short sleeves; lower body in a neatly pleated white cotton dhoti, wrapped and knotted at the front in Satavahana-period Andhra style, reaching to the ankles; bare feet are avoided—he wears simple brown leather sandals with thong straps; around his waist a narrow reddish-brown cotton sash is tied once to hold tools; on his wrists plain bronze bangles, and a single small cylindrical crystal bead pendant hangs from a thin dark thread necklace, evoking modest donor status without royal grandeur; no elaborate crown or heavy jewellery, just restrained, plausible ornaments in keeping with a middle-ranking artisan-donor.
appearance.signature: A long, pale limestone relief panel held under one arm, its surface partly carved with delicate lotus medallions and stupa rail motifs, while in his right hand he grips a short iron chisel and a wooden mallet, tools resting lightly rather than raised to strike.

ref_desc: An early-30s medium-brown Amaravati sculptor-donor with an oval face, short beard, black hair tied in a low knot and white headband, wearing off-white uttariya, beige under-tunic, white dhoti, bronze bangles, sandals, carrying a pale limestone relief panel with chisel and mallet in a reddish-brown sash palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body shonen-anime style male character from ancient Andhra Pradesh as a consistent model sheet: an early-30s medium-brown Amaravati sculptor-donor with an oval face, straight nose, sharp kind eyes, and a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, his thick black hair combed back into a short low knot at the nape and held by a narrow white cotton headband around the forehead. He wears an era-accurate off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and across the chest, covering a light beige short-sleeved under-tunic, with a white cotton dhoti wrapped and pleated to the ankles in Satavahana-period Andhra style, plus simple brown leather sandals. A narrow reddish-brown sash circles his waist, holding modest tools, and he has plain bronze bangles on his wrists and a tiny cylindrical crystal bead pendant on a thin dark thread necklace, suggesting a modest donor without royal regalia. In his left arm he cradles a long pale limestone relief panel partially carved with lotus medallions and stupa rail motifs, while in his right hand he loosely holds a short iron chisel and a wooden mallet. Use an authentic, subdued palette of off-white, light beige, reddish-brown, bronze, and pale stone, and show him front-facing with clear details of face, hair, garments, jewellery, tools, and stone panel so this design can be redrawn identically in every panel.
